zh: k≥2 时，不超过 10^18 的 k 的正整数次幂最多只有约 60 个（k=2 时 2^1..2^59）。
先把这些幂全部生成出来放进一张表（集合），再逐个检查数组元素是否在表里即可，不需要对每个元素做分解或取对数。
从 p=k 开始不断乘 k，每次乘之前先判断 p>10^18/k，成立就停止，避免溢出；10^18 在有符号 64 位范围内。不要用浮点对数判断，精度会出错。元素都至少为 2，所以 k^0=1 不需要考虑。最后统计命中个数。
en: For k >= 2 there are at most about 60 positive powers of k not exceeding 10^18 (2^1..2^59 when k = 2).
Generate all of these powers into a table (a set) first, then check whether each array element is in the table; no factoring or logarithms per element are needed.

Start from p = k and keep multiplying by k; before each multiplication check p > 10^18 / k and stop if so, which avoids overflow (10^18 fits in a signed 64-bit integer). Do not decide with floating-point logarithms, since the precision fails. All elements are at least 2, so k^0 = 1 never matters. Count the hits.

explanationEn:
## Problem

Given an array arr and an integer k, count how many numbers in arr are powers of k (k^1, k^2, ...). In this problem both k and the elements of arr are at least 2.

## Approach

For k >= 2 there are at most 60 powers of k not exceeding 10^18. First generate all the powers by starting from k and repeatedly multiplying by k; before each multiplication check p > 10^18/k to see whether it would exceed the bound, which avoids overflow. Then check whether each element is in this table.

## Correctness

All elements are >= 2, so k^0=1 never occurs; the generated table contains exactly all positive powers <= 10^18. Comparing element by element gives the count.

## Complexity

O(n*log_k 10^18), at most about 60n comparisons.

## Independent verification

The oracle repeatedly divides each element by k until it is no longer divisible, and the element is a power if what remains is 1 (Python big integers, no overflow); this differs from the reference's power-table approach. All arrays of length 1..3 with k=2..4 and elements 2..20 were exhausted, running the reference program on each. The formal cases include powers and non-powers close to 10^18 (such as 10^18-1), a very large k with only its first power, all 60 powers of k=2, and so on. The wrong solutions cover floating-point logarithms, checking only divisibility, looking only at the first and second powers, and 32-bit input.
